title: Recorded lichen richness gaps closed mainly through control losses after nitrogen addition stopped at Culardoch
abstract: We tested lichen recovery after nitrogen addition stopped at Culardoch, Scotland. We used a 2026 release of 96 plots surveyed in 17 years. Two inconsistent design strata were excluded, leaving 22 matched high-dose and control pairs. Between 2008-2010 and 2021, the recorded taxon deficit fell from 5.15 to 0.86 per plot. Treated richness changed by -0.18 taxa (conditional 95% bootstrap limits -0.91 to 0.59), while control richness fell by 4.47 (3.32 to 5.68). Genus counts gave a similar result. A 1.35 percentage point cover deficit remained eleven years after addition stopped (adjusted randomization p = 0.0114). Some recovery appeared when only taxa with at least 0.5% cover were counted. Thus a smaller recorded richness deficit did not establish restoration. This exploratory analysis adds an independent experimental constraint on community memory and an exact split of gap closure. One site, changing detection, rescued metadata and a six-year survey gap limit inference. It does not identify soil or dispersal mechanisms or measure the climate-tracking gap. Raw records remain external; code, aggregate results, figures and source hashes are included.
